source.title: "Moram uspjeti" - Vrijedim li ako nisam uspješan? ⎸ EHOCAST

summary.title_hr: "Moram uspjeti" - Vrijedim li ako nisam uspješan? ⎸ EHOCAST
summary.abstract_hr: U ovoj epizodi EHOCAST-a voditelj Marko razgovara s Franom iz Molitvene zajednice Eho i Mislavom, poznatim na društvenim mrežama kao Tata Hrast, o tome što za muškarca znači uspjeh i kako se uspjeh povezuje s novcem, karijerom i vlastitom vrijednošću. Sugovornici opisuju svoje dječje predodžbe o uspjehu, očekivanja koja društvo stavlja pred muškarce te zamku uspoređivanja s drugima. Mislav govori o tome kako je vlastitu vrijednost mjerio zaradom i živio u modu preživljavanja, a nakon upozorenja supruge i rođenja kćeri smanjio je posao za 70% kako bi imao više vremena za obitelj. Fran svjedoči o desetini i Božjoj providnosti, a Marko o identitetu, služenju u zajednici i odlučivanju u skladu s Božjom voljom uz suprugu. Zaključuju da je uspjeh biti najbolji gdje god jesi, staviti Boga na prvo mjesto, graditi zdrave obiteljske odnose i jasno odrediti kakav život želiš živjeti.
key_points: Mislav je odrastao uz obiteljske napetosti koje su uglavnom bile vezane uz novac, pa je kao odrasla osoba živio u modu preživljavanja i vlastitu vrijednost mjerio iznosom koji može zaraditi za obitelj. Kao hiperambiciozan čovjek stalno je postavljao nove ciljeve i postao najveći kritičar samome sebi.

Supruga mu je rekla da im svi novci ovog svijeta nisu dovoljni ako oni nisu dobro, što mu je bio poziv na buđenje. Nakon rođenja kćeri smanjio je posao i prihode za 70% kako bi dobio vrijeme za obitelj, a pokazalo se da i uz 70% manje rada može ostvariti iste prihode.
Mislav ističe da osigurati obitelj ne znači samo financirati je, jer je prihod samo jedna stavka uz odnose, stabilnost i sigurnost koju muškarac pruža supruzi i djeci.

Fran je kao dijete uspješnog oca vidio u svom tati, ratnom invalidu koji je uvijek bio kod kuće, a životni cilj mu je oduvijek bio imati obitelj i biti otac. Ispričao je kako je, unatoč skromnim primanjima, počeo davati desetinu te je taj mjesec dobio višestruko više novca i posao, a vodi se riječima iz Mateja 6: »Tražite najprije kraljevstvo Božje.«

Marko je od djetinjstva sanjao o korporaciji, bankama i odijelima, ali se posvetio radu u zajednici i završio teologiju. Ističe da se i u neprofitnom sektoru mora raditi na bračnim i obiteljskim odnosima te da ga supruga Mirjana kod svake nove ideje pita je li siguran da to Bog želi od njega.
Sugovornici upozoravaju na zamku uspoređivanja s ljudima koji su desetak godina stariji. Smatraju da svatko ima drugačiju početnu točku i svoj put, iako možda svi idu prema istom cilju.

Kao zaključak navode da treba biti najbolji gdje god se nalaziš, staviti Boga na prvo mjesto i zapitati se kakav život želiš živjeti. Dodaju da je u redu tražiti pomoć i savjet od drugih, a zajedništvo i ravnopravnost sa supružnikom Mislav naziva najvećim životnim uspjehom muškarca.
key_points_en: Mislav grew up with family tensions that were mostly related to money, so as an adult he lived in survival mode and measured his own self-worth by the amount he could earn for his family. As a hyper-ambitious man, he constantly set new goals and became his own greatest critic.

His wife told him that all the money in this world is not enough for them if they are not well, which served as a wake-up call for him. After the birth of his daughter, he reduced his work and income by 70% in order to gain time for his family, and it turned out that even with 70% less work he could achieve the same income.

Mislav emphasizes that providing for a family does not only mean financing it, because income is only one item alongside relationships, stability, and the security that a man provides to his wife and children.

As a child, Fran saw a successful father in his dad, a disabled war veteran who was always at home, and his life goal had always been to have a family and be a father. He recounted how, despite modest income, he began giving a tithe and that month received multiple times more money and a job, guided by the words from Matthew 6: "Seek first the kingdom of God."

From childhood, Marko dreamed of corporations, banks, and suits, but he dedicated himself to work in the community and completed theology. He emphasizes that even in the non-profit sector one must work on marital and family relationships, and that with every new idea his wife Mirjana asks him if he is sure that God wants that from him.

The interlocutors warn against the trap of comparing oneself to people who are ten or so years older. They believe that everyone has a different starting point and their own path, even though everyone might be heading toward the same goal.

In conclusion, they state that one should be the best wherever one is, put God in first place, and ask oneself what kind of life one wants to live. They add that it is okay to seek help and advice from others, and Mislav calls fellowship and equality with one's spouse a man's greatest success in life.
summary.title_en: "I Must Succeed" - Am I Worth Anything If I Am Not Successful? ⎸ EHOCAST
summary.abstract_en: In this episode of EHOCAST, host Marko speaks with Fran from the Molitvena zajednica Eho and Mislav, known on social media as Tata Hrast, about what success means for a man and how success is connected to money, career, and one's own self-worth. The interlocutors describe their childhood ideas of success, the expectations that society places on men, and the trap of comparing oneself to others. Mislav talks about how he measured his own self-worth by earnings and lived in survival mode, and after his wife's warning and the birth of his daughter, he reduced his work by 70% in order to have more time for his family. Fran testifies about tithing and God's providence, and Marko about identity, serving in the community, and making decisions in accordance with God's will alongside his wife. They conclude that success is being the best wherever you are, putting God in first place, building healthy family relationships, and clearly defining what kind of life you want to live.
